item.title: Latvia’s border guard seeks greater powers amid increasingly violent border crossings
item.description: As “armed, masked escorts” lead migrants from Belarus into Latvia, the Latvian Border Guard is seeking greater powers to “protect Latvia’s security.” The interior minister supports the proposal.

item.title: EU calls US sanctions on International Criminal Court 'regrettable'
item.description: The ICC was established to prosecute war crimes and crimes against humanity that might otherwise go unpunished.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 9th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 9th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Former Prince Andrew receives £302,000 for surrendering royal lease
item.description: After leaving Royal Lodge in February, Prince Andrew moved to a property on the Sandringham Estate in eastern England, which is privately owned by King Charles III.

item.title: Which European countries are winning the tech funding race?
item.description: Investment in European tech startups is rebounding after a slow summer, but remains unevenly spread with the UK capturing almost half of all funding, according to figures from tech.eu.

item.title: Iran's IRGC strikes tanker and threatens to target vessels beyond Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard warned that vessels “violating” its designated routes would be pursued and "punished" anywhere in the region, as maritime agencies reported two further strikes on commercial ships in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: UN voices 'concern' over violence as French students plan more protests
item.description: 141 of France's 3,700 high schools were closed on Friday, according to the Education Ministry.

item.title: Tornadoes sweep across Sicily, leaving flipped cars and damaged buildings
item.description: A rare double waterspout formed off the coast of Marsala in western Sicily on 9 October, before moving inland and causing significant damage.

item.title: EU and China clinch deal over cars after heated trade talks as Brussels pushes to rebalance trade
item.description: EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič described the deal as marking the end of the “first phase” of negotiations. Brussels is pushing for a fundamental rebalancing in trade relations with Beijing.

item.title: Thieves in Italy target prestigious winemaker, making off with €5 million haul: reports
item.description: Antinori dates back to 1385 and is one of Italy's most renowned winemakers. The company has reportedly warned customers to look out for offers of its wines coming from outside of official channels.

item.title: Sounds of Mexico brings Mexican orchestral music to Doha
item.description: The Qatar Philharmonic brings the sounds of Mexico to Doha, with musicians from around the world exploring Mexican orchestral traditions.

item.title: The second time around: Meet the men who run the pre-owned luxury watch market
item.description: After thousands of people queued around the world earlier this year to get their hands on the avant-garde Audemars Piguet x Swatch, Royal Pop collaboration, collectors have been carefully following the second-hand market. Now, two leading watch experts share their secrets of what and when to buy.

item.title: Indonesia: Baby orangutan saved from Borneo wildfires as habitat destruction escalates
item.description: A young orangutan has been rescued from wildfires in Borneo. Named Novita, the three- to four-year-old female was found clinging to a tree in Central Kalimantan on 26 September, with burns to her hands and feet after crossing the flames.

item.title: Helsinki votes in favour of banning fossil fuel adverts – but there could be a 10-year delay
item.description: “Cities can’t keep working to cut emissions while allowing their own advertising spaces to encourage more flying and fossil fuel consumption.”

item.title: Police and protesters clash in Brussels as anti-austerity rally disrupts city
item.description: Police and protesters clashed in Brussels on Friday as tens of thousands of people rallied separately in the Belgian capital against rising living costs and budget-tightening measures introduced by the government.

item.title: Three in four EU workers face suspicious emails and links, report finds
item.description: Phishing remains the most common cyber threat — only one in two respondents say they are able to spot a deepfake video.

item.title: Virgin unveils new train designs and plans for cross-Channel service linking London and Europe from 2030
item.description: The company plans to launch 20 daily return services linking London with Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam, and wants to bring its signature hospitality to the service.

item.title: 35 killed in strikes on Ukraine's Donetsk region as Russia reports four dead across Belgorod
item.description: Zelenskyy announced on Friday that Ukrainian forces had also carried out a strike on a "major" Russian oil refinery in Omsk, as well as striking another refinery in Ukhta.

item.title: EU paid €7.9bn for Russian Arctic LNG amid record imports
item.description: Continued Russian LNG imports undermine the credibility of the EU’s promise to sever its energy ties with Moscow, particularly as Russia continues its war against Ukraine.

item.title: Seals and sea lions undergo hearing tests in Australian research
item.description: Australia's scientists have trained seals and sea lions to take hearing tests at Sydney's Taronga Zoo, hoping to better understand how human-made noise affects marine mammals.

item.title: Electrification and Chinese brands: Paris Motor Show opens Monday
item.description: As the 91st Paris Motor Show draws near, European carmakers face fierce competition from China, waning confidence and mounting geopolitical pressures.

item.title: Spain: Madrid protesters mourn evicted pensioner Maricarmen Abascal
item.description: Tens of thousands marched in Madrid to mourn pensioner Maricarmen Abascal, whose eviction made her a housing crisis symbol and sparked fresh protests.

item.title: After the foldable iPhone, Apple’s next launch could come to your home
item.description: Apple has teased a new smart home launch just 10 days before iPhone Duo arrives. Here’s what we might see.

item.title: The Hague wants a kill switch for EU police data-sharing with third countries
item.description: The Netherlands wants EU police data-sharing with trusted non-EU countries, including candidates, to be terminable after a ‘radical change of regime’.

item.title: Interpol operation seized 2,800 illegal firearms across Europe and Asia
item.description: An Interpol-coordinated operation conducted across 17 countries in Europe and Asia this summer allowed the seizure of 2,823 firearms and over 40,000 pieces of ammunition.

item.title: Passport-free travel, AI agents and longevity: Key takeaways from the WTTC Global Summit
item.description: The 26th edition of the World Travel & Tourism Council Global Summit just concluded in Malta – here’s what you may have missed from the ‘Davos of travel’.

item.title: What happened to OpenAI’s $20bn? Revenue scare rattles AI trade
item.description: US tech futures rebounded on Friday, a day after a report that OpenAI’s annualised revenue was $20 billion (€17.8bn) below earlier estimates helped send the Nasdaq down 1.25% and hit chipmakers and cloud giants.

item.title: Iran and Russia used ChatGPT for propaganda by ‘fake journalists’, OpenAI says
item.description: The American tech giant said it banned Russian and Iranian accounts that had been using ChatGPT models to generate content and fake journalist personas to spread false narratives about the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East and sow division.

item.title: Putin offers help to end Iran war while Russia continues its own in Ukraine
item.description: The Russian president met Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan and pledged to do “everything in our power” to end the ongoing war between the US and Iran, despite Russia not being among the official mediators.

item.title: In Pictures: Weirdest and most thought-provoking statues of Donald Trump over the years
item.description: Following the headline-grabbing statue "The Orange Plague" by Danish artist Jens Galschiøt, which was displayed this week at the European Parliament building in Strasbourg, we take a look back at some of the ways artists have depicted Trump in satirical, humorous and thought-provoking ways.

item.title: 'Grand odysseys': Why historic travel and legendary journeys are trending for 2027
item.description: Skyscanner’s 2027 travel trends report points to growing demand for historic trails, ancient ruins and iconic destinations brought to life on screen, as travellers look to the past for a sense of connection in a fast-paced world.

item.title: Inside Kazakhstan’s historic rock-hewn mosques now recognised by UNESCO
item.description: Five rock-hewn mosques and associated sacred sites dating from the 12th to the 18th centuries make up Kazakhstan’s newest UNESCO World Heritage property. The complexes preserve centuries of Sufi tradition alongside much older beliefs.

item.title: ‘I still want to verify this’: Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay’s first reaction
item.description: Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, 85, said she initially thought the news was a joke when she learned she had won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. The former judge said she wanted to verify the announcement before believing it.

item.title: Ukrainian and European officials fly to Miami for US-led peace talks
item.description: The US is hosting a round of peace talks in Miami with Ukrainian and European officials. President Zelenskyy aims to secure a targeted ceasefire that can cover either the Black Sea, energy facilities or both.

item.title: Former Ilva steelworkers to strike as shutdown threatens thousands of jobs in Italy
item.description: Acciaierie d'Italia has announced a suspension of production in Taranto pending a ruling from Italy's Supreme Court of Cassation, with plants in Genoa and Novi Ligure also set to shut down temporarily by 15 November.

item.title: EU countries agree to shift oversight of major financial markets to European authority ESMA
item.description: EU countries struck a deal on Friday to give the EU’s financial markets watchdog more powers, aiming to make cross-border investment easier and help businesses raise more money across the bloc.

item.title: Narrow body jets will ‘change the shape of travel’, says Dubai Airports CEO
item.description: Speaking on the sidelines of the WTTC Global Summit in Malta, Dubai Airports chief Paul Griffiths shared that he believes the expansion of regional airports will be key in the next decade of travel.

item.title: Death in Russian lab raises questions over plague pathogen bioweapon research
item.description: The US accuse Russia and other states of developing banned biological weapons. After an incident at the plague lab in Irkutsk, Euronews interviewed bioweapons expert Mirko Himmel.

item.title: Houthi missile strikes on Riyadh airport kill three, including airline captain
item.description: Two missile strikes on King Khalid International Airport forced diplomats to shelter in place and delayed dozens of flights, as Yemen’s government claimed progress in its Red Sea counter-offensive. Houthi forces said they were holding their ground.

item.title: Left-wing candidate Hitler Mussolini wins local vote in Peru
item.description: Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores won by 25 votes in Queropalca, a district of just over 730 people in the Huánuco department, running for the centre-left Ahora Nación party. He is not Peru’s first elected Hitler.

item.title: Frozen testicular tissue transplanted in bid to restore fertility after chemotherapy
item.description: Protecting fertility is a major challenge for young men undergoing aggressive treatments such as chemotherapy. Freezing their own testicular tissue before such treatments could help.

item.title: German logistics group Rhenus plans up to 14 terminals along the Middle Corridor
item.description: Global logistics company Rhenus Group plans to build a new multimodal hub in the Kazakh city of Aktau and develop up to 14 terminals along the Middle Corridor. This network will link Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Türkiye, and connect the route to the company's infrastructure in Europe.

item.title: French authorities arrests at least five people over €9 million theft from Renoir Museum
item.description: The suspects are believed to include the two alleged burglars, who reportedly broke into the museum at dawn by cutting through a fence.

item.title: Intense diplomatic manoeuvring in Athens over first Russian team in European tournament
item.description: The Kazan club was the first Russian club to play an official European club match in Greece, after discreet pressure to keep Russian symbols out of the Serafio pool.

item.title: Greece is the most popular luxury honeymoon destination for 2027 – with Italy and France also in the top 10
item.description: Greece tops the ranking of the world’s most popular honeymoon destinations for 2027 in Virtuoso’s latest Luxe Report, ahead of Bali and the Maldives.

item.title: Jurist Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for 2026
item.description: Announcing the award, Jørgen Watne Frydnes, the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee, said it was going to a "person who with exceptional courage and integrity has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order."

item.title: Violence is 'not general' in French students protests, MEP says
item.description: French S&D MEP Emma Rafowicz says Emmanuel Macron’s government is “completely irresponsible” in its handling of the ongoing student protests in France.

item.title: Scientific study reveals scariest horror movie – with one 2026 title breaking heart rate record
item.description: The ranking was determined by a study monitoring audience's heart rates and BPM increases while watching horror films.

item.title: Associate EU membership 'very interesting' for New Zealand, says former prime minister
item.description: Helen Clark, former prime minister of New Zealand, says a form of associate membership of the European Union, similar to the proposal for Canada, would be “very interesting”. She highlights access to the single market as a potential key benefit for a “distant trading country” such as New Zealand.

item.title: Police arrest suspect after deadly shooting in Germany's Upper Palatinate
item.description: A 60-year-old is alleged to have shot and killed a male and a female employee of the Neumarkt District Office during a routine weapons check.
